messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Turkish, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Turkish line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Şimdi sen o Virgil ve o kaynak mısın ki konuşmanın bu kadar geniş bir nehrini yayar mı, Ben ona utangaç bir alınla cevap verdim.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|------------------|--------| | Or | temporal marker “Now/then” | **Şimdi** | “now” | OK | | se' | copular verb “art” (2 sg.) | **mısın** | “are (you)?” | OK | | tu | 2 sg. pronoun “thou” | **sen** | “you” | OK | | quel | demonstrative “that” (modifying *Virgilio*) | **o** | “that” | OK | | Virgilio | proper noun “Virgil” | **Virgil** | “Virgil” | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | **ve** | “and” | OK | | quella | demonstrative “that” (modifying *fonte*) | **o** | “that” | OK | | fonte | noun “fount / source” | **kaynak** | “source” | OK | | che | relative pronoun “which / that” | **ki** | “that” (introducing clause) | OK | | spandi | verb “poureth forth” | **yayar** | “spreads / pours forth” | OK | | di | preposition “of” (genitive) | *(genitive suffix in “konuşmanın”)* | “of” | **UNNECESSARY** (Turkish marks genitive with a suffix, no separate word) | | parlar | noun “speech” (infinitive used substantively) | **konuşmanın** | “of speech” | OK | | sì | degree adverb “so” | **bu kadar** | “so / this much” | OK | | largo | adjective “large” | **geniş** | “large” | OK | | fiume | noun “river / stream” | **nehrini** | “river (acc.)” | OK | | rispuos' | verb “replied” | **verdim** | “I replied” | OK | | io | 1 sg. pronoun “I” | **Ben** | “I” | OK | | lui | 3 sg. indirect object “to him” | **ona** | “to him” | OK | | con | preposition “with” (instrumental) | *(instrumental suffix in “alınla”)* | “with” | **UNNECESSARY** (instrumental expressed by suffix) | | vergognosa | adjective “bashful” | **utangaç** | “bashful” | OK | | fronte | noun “front (of the face)” | **alın** | “forehead / front” | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention - **di** – marked **UNNECESSARY** (Turkish encodes the genitive relationship inside the word *konuşmanın*; no separate preposition is needed). - **con** – marked **UNNECESSARY** (the instrumental meaning is expressed by the suffix *‑la* in *alınla*; no separate word is required).
No source words are **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or suffering **GRAMMAR** mismatches in the Turkish rendering.
